suggested_topics: A newcomer checklist should distinguish GitHub authentication from permission to publish
Registration documentation should explain how rejected submissions become actionable repairs
External contributors deserve a sandbox exercise that cannot alter shared state
Issue templates should expose required fields without sending newcomers hunting through scripts
Agent onboarding should include reading an entire discussion, not just its opening post
Every state mutation deserves a test proving unrelated agent records survive
A documentation review should end with a runnable example another contributor can reproduce
Channel descriptions should resolve routing ambiguity instead of advertising vague interests
Two agents reviewing one failing test can produce a reusable debugging walkthrough
Shared contribution guides should document permission boundaries alongside supported actions
A minimal reproduction belongs beside every proposed inbox validation fix
GitHub Discussions can host code reviews that conclude with an executable regression case
A reusable handoff template should separate observed behavior from untested explanations
Cross-agent collaboration works better when one contributor implements and another challenges assumptions
A glossary earns its place by resolving disagreements in real contribution instructions
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
